newsitem.title: USA: New cargo building opens at Miami International.
newsitem.headline: New cargo building opens at Miami International.

text.p: The first of three buildings of a new $67.8 million Miami International Airport cargo facility opened Monday.
"When you look at our cargo projections, you can see why these buildings are so important to Miami," Gary Dellapa, director of the airport, said at the opening ceremony Monday .

MIA is expected to handle 1.8 million tons of cargo this year, with 85 percent of that international, Dellapa said. Next year MIA officials expect that to rise to two million tons, and to three million tons by the year 2000, Dellappa said.

The new facility, referred to as the Western U, is made up of three buildings and will total 597,000 square feet of office and warehouse space when completed, according to the Metro-Dade Aviation department. It will have parking space for 12 aircraft or eight Boeing 747s.
The first tenants at the new building are LanChile and Fast Air Cargo.

MIA is about half way through a $500 million cargo development program and has completed eight new cargo cargo buildings with 1.2 million square feet. In the next four years about one million more square feet will be completed.
